title: CVTA: Cross-Variable Temporal Attention for Multivariate Irregular Time Series Prediction
claim: One irregular input can be modeled through several distinct attention paradigms, each processing the same observations differently.
layout: 4 panels; input top-left with arrows fanning out to three attention variants
description: Four boxed panels with light-blue title bars. The top-left panel shows an irregular multivariate time series: four dashed colored lines (green, blue, red, orange) with filled dots for observations and question-mark dots for the values to predict. Thick black arrows lead from it to three panels. Top-right, "Attention via Msg. Passing", shows two grey ovals of nodes joined by dotted edges with envelope icons for messages. Bottom-left, "Attention over Obs.", shows reference points with dotted attention arrows going to individual observations. Bottom-right, "Attention over Patches", shows color-coded temporal patches feeding a patch-embedding box and then an attention-over-patches box. Dotted legend boxes sit in the corners. The eye goes first to the input series and then follows the arrows.
caption: Overview of attention-based architectures for irregular multivariate time series prediction. Irregularly sampled multivariate observations (top left) can be modeled using different attention mechanisms: point-wise attention (bottom left) applies attention directly to individual observations; patch-based attention (bottom right) aggregates observations into temporal patches before applying attention; and structured message passing (top right) represents time points and variables as nodes in graphs or hypergraphs and learns attention via message passing.
abstract: Irregularly sampled multivariate time series arise in many real-world domains such as healthcare, climate science, and large-scale monitoring systems. Characterized by asynchronous observations and heterogeneity across variables, such time series pose significant challenges for forecasting. In this work, we introduce Cross-Variable Temporal Attention (CVTA), a short-term, continuous-time forecasting framework that learns prediction functions from its compact, interpretable state summarizing recent temporal dynamics across variables. CVTA uses Variable-Conditioned Embeddings to project heterogeneous variables into variable-specific latent spaces, and applies temporal attention to capture cross-variable dependencies from this state. Furthermore, we demonstrate that CVTA can be integrated as an auxiliary module into existing state-of-the-art prediction models through a dynamic meta-decision model. Extensive experiments on multiple real-world benchmarks show that CVTA achieves strong short-term predictive accuracy, supports efficient online inference, improves existing prediction models when used as an auxiliary module, and learns attention patterns that align well with domain knowledge.
